item.title: Bandai-Azuma Skyline & Nishi-Azuma Sky Valley: Fukushima's Great Scenic Drives — Guide
item.description: The Bandai-Azuma Skyline and the neighbouring Nishi-Azuma Sky Valley are two of Tohoku’s most celebrated scenic mountain drives, winding roughly 30 km combined through the volcanic Azuma range at elevations over 1,600 m. Each curve reveals a new lookout over jagged peaks, steaming volcanic vents and, come October, some of the region’s most vivid autumn foliage — a fiery tapestry of maple and beech that draws road-trippers from across Japan. Both routes are seasonal toll roads, closed by snow each winter.

item.title: Narugo Gorge & Naruko Onsen: Autumn Colours & Kokeshi Dolls — Guide
item.description: Narugo Gorge erupts in some of Tohoku’s finest autumn colour each October and November — a 2 km ravine where the Narugo River has cut through volcanic rock to create vertical walls of deep red maple, yellow ginkgo and ochre oak reflected in the dark river below. The adjoining hot-spring town of Naruko is Japan’s kokeshi doll capital, with 11 different spring water types and dozens of craft workshops where visitors can watch masters turn painted wooden dolls on a lathe.

item.title: Ranzan Gorge: A Quiet Riverside Walk Named for Kyoto's Arashiyama — Guide
item.description: Ranzan Gorge takes its name from a Confucian scholar who, upon seeing the valley’s forested slopes along a tributary of the Arakawa River, was reminded of Kyoto’s celebrated Arashiyama district. The gorge offers a gentler, quieter alternative to Saitama’s more famous nature spots, with an easy riverside walking path through mixed forest that turns especially vivid during autumn foliage season, making it a relaxed half-day nature escape within reach of Tokyo.

item.title: Yamadera (Risshakuji Temple): 1,015 Steps to Silence — Guide
item.description: Yamadera (Risshakuji Temple) is one of Japan’s most dramatic temple complexes — clinging to sheer cliffs above the valley, reached by climbing 1,015 stone steps carved into the mountainside. Haiku master Matsuo Basho visited in 1689 and composed his famous verse on the silence here. The view from the Godaido platform is extraordinary in every season, especially in autumn’s crimson and gold. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Yamadera, Yamagata Hours ~8:00–17:00 Admission Around ¥600 Time needed 1.

item.title: Kyoto Autumn Foliage Guide: The Best Momiji Spots & Timing
item.description: Autumn may be Kyoto at its most beautiful. For a few magical weeks each November, the city’s maples (momiji) turn fiery red, orange, and gold, setting temple halls, gardens, hillsides, and rivers ablaze with colour. The Japanese love of koyo (autumn leaves) rivals their devotion to cherry blossom, and Kyoto — with its hundreds of temples framed by maples — is the country’s premier destination to enjoy it. This guide covers when the foliage peaks, the very best places to see it, the spectacular night illuminations, and how to plan around the considerable crowds.

item.title: Nishiyama Trail Guide: Kyoto's Quiet Western Mountains
item.description: Most visitors never set foot in Nishiyama — the wooded western mountains of Kyoto — and that is exactly its appeal. While the eastern hills heave with tour groups, this quiet range of bamboo forests, hillside temples, and country lanes offers some of the city’s most peaceful temple-going and gentle hiking, crowned by the sprawling mountainside temple of Yoshimine-dera with its sweeping views over the Kyoto basin. For travellers who have already seen the headline sights and want the Kyoto that locals keep for themselves, Nishiyama is a rewarding escape.
